### Axioms as directions, in one animation

<p align="center"><img src="{{fig:axiom_arrows_qwen3.5-2b.gif}}" alt="Pairs of group-like structures that differ in one axiom, drawn as 3-D arrows that slide to one common origin; Qwen3.5-2B left, its random-init twin right" width="720"></p>

- **What you see:** the 13 group-like structures (magma, unital magma, quasigroup, loop, semigroup, monoid, group, and the commutative versions of all but the unital magma) in the top-3 principal components of Qwen3.5-2B (left) and of its random-init twin (right), at the preregistered layer. One axiom at a time, every pair of structures that differ only in that axiom becomes an arrow, for example monoid → commutative monoid and group → abelian group for commutativity. The arrows then slide to one common origin, so you can see whether they point the same way.
- **What to notice:** in the trained model the commutativity arrows form one bundle. Their offset consistency, the mean cosine between the {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.n_pairs}} difference vectors in the full residual stream, is {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.consistency:.2f}}. The twin's is {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b__random.group_like.offsets.commutative.consistency:.2f}}, and random pairs of the same structures exceed {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.null95:.2f}} only 5% of the time. Associativity behaves the same way ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.associative.consistency:.2f}}, twin {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b__random.group_like.offsets.associative.consistency:.2f}}). Identity ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.identity.consistency:.2f}}) and divisibility ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.divisible.consistency:.2f}}) form looser bundles.
- **Caveat:** three principal components can hide or exaggerate parallelism, so the statistic is computed in the full space, never from this picture. In Qwen3.5-2B only associativity and commutativity survive Holm correction; identity and divisibility are significant before correction only (the scorecard below has every model).
